newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan tenders to buy Jul-Sep oil products.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan tenders to buy Jul-Sep oil products.

text.p: Pakistan's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources has issued a tender to buy various oil products for July-September deliveries which amounted to less than its purchases in the second quarter tender, an industry source said on Thursday.
The tender seeks 300,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil on a fixed basis, and another 240,000 tonnes on an optional basis, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) to Keamari.
It also seeks 360,000 tonnes of 180-centistoke grade, 3.5-percent sulphur furnace or fuel oil on a fixed basis, and another 360,000 tonnes on an optional basis, c-and-f Fotco.
Pakistan also seeks 100,000 tonnes of 180-cst, 1.0-percent sulphur furnace oil on a fixed basis and another 50,000 tonnes on an optional basis, c-and-f Keamari.
The tender closes on May 31 and offers will be valid until June 10, the source said.
He said the lesser volume slated for the third quarter is due to the monsoon season as hydropower would meet demand from power plants rather than fuel oil.
Diesel imports would also be curbed due to a lull in sowing and harvesting activities. "But the optional cargoes would cover the demand when the monsoon fluctuates," he said.
Pakistan purchased a total of 450,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel in its last tender for the second quarter from Saudi-based trader Bakri Trading.
The award was between 84 cents and $1.14 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f Keamari.

It also bought 400,000 tonnes of 180-cst, 3.5-percent sulphur fuel oil from Bakri Trading and Sharjah Oil Refining Co and 300,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur fuel oil from Bakro Trading and Dutch trader Vitol and Swiss trader Glencore.

The 3.5-percent grade fuel oil was awarded between $11.76 and $11.80 per tonne above MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f Fotco and the 1.0-percent sulphur grade was between $44 and $49.50 per tonne above MidEast quotes, c-and-f Keamari.
